title: "Ode to a Giant" and Eddie Laguna's small concerts
summary: He explains the blues made up on the spot for the Sunset label and talks of small concerts recorded without commercial thought.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: This listing came from Rust. Earlier we were looking at the listings for you in the Jepsen discography, and you were going to talk about some of the things that you found there that you said you had forgotten you did.

Oh, yeah. I'm looking here, The Red Callender Six. That was with Herbie Haymer, Arnold Ross, Les Paul, Shadow Wilson. That's when we did "These Foolish Things" and an original, "Ode To A Giant," "Get Happy" featuring Sweets Edison, "I Cover The Waterfront" which featured Sweets, and "Lady, Be Good."
"Ode To A Giant" was a thing based on the Blues, put together right on the spot.
Where did the title come from?
Eddie Laguna probably dreamed up that title? Remember Eddie Laguna?
Yes, I remember Eddie Laguna. He was a neighbor of mine.
That was his label, the Sunset label.
That's right. And one time he was partners with Gene Norman -- later on, I think.

Right. Yeah, we did a lot of things. We mentioned that briefly before. Because we used to play a lot of concerts around, and they recorded all these things. We weren't particularly aware of... We knew they were recording them, but we had no idea it was for future commercial use. Neither did they. It's just that they realized at the time that so much good music is never heard because it's never recorded. Some of the best things have never been recorded, so we've missed so much music.
They were promoting small Jazz concerts around town.
Very small. Sometimes Eddie would get these little theaters.
That's right, very small. Even school auditoriums.
